outcome.technical: VERB (audit-task.py): `skill-pin <name> [--source TEXT] [--allow-personal-copy] [--reason TEXT]` and `skill-pin <name> --remove --reason TEXT`, wired as the verb table's sibling of build-command: usage block, VERB_FLAGS row (skill_source, allow_personal_copy, remove, reason), parser choice and two flags, doors map, `import _skill_places`. It computes nothing of its own: resolve_skill places the name, skill_digest digests the whole directory, loaded_verdict says a personal copy does not travel, covering_pins finds the pins already holding the directory, _manifest_rules.skill_pin_findings is asked of the plan as it will be written. Under the plan's lock (_under_lock), written through _write_plan (index-only, revalidated, rolled back), journaled as skillpin.change (field, from, to, reason; changes[] when more than one spelling moved). Refusals, each exit 2 with nothing written and the reader's words: a string that is no skill name, a name nothing places (every place looked in), a directory with no digest (entry and kind), a personal copy without --allow-personal-copy (with the flag it pins and warns), --remove with no reason, --remove of a name not pinned (naming the spelling that is), --remove beside --source, a --source carrying a machine path; a plan already holding two pins on one directory with different digests is refused with exit 1 and the validator's finding (and a --remove of one is let through). A matching pin changes nothing and says so; a changed one prints old and new digest; --source alone is a 'source updated'; a directory pinned under another spelling has THAT pin updated (never a second); the last pin removed takes the skillPins key with it. DOCTOR (_doctor_policy.py): check_plan_skills is now two calls - _plan_skills_resolve (the old body, which returns early) and the new _plan_skill_pins - so the pin rows do not depend on the scan. Rows check 'skill pins', only when the plan carries a non-empty skillPins: matches (path) as one OK row; mismatch / not found / unreadable are WARNINGs worded by _skill_places.stop_words over pin_verdict (the runner's own sentence, naming a tool-written entry) with a fix saying a session naming it will not start; shape problems and directory clashes warn; stale pins (unused_pins) warn; plan skills nothing pins (covering_pins) are an OK row; a project skill's working copy that differs from HEAD (git status --porcelain over the directory) says the commit is what a wave's sessions load, and a matching one that differs is a WARNING.
